title: On the Limits of Scale: Inverse Scaling in Vision-Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.27360v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Scaling laws suggest that increasing model size, training data, and compute generally yields monotonic performance improvements. While this often holds at the aggregate level, we present systematic evidence that vision-language models (VLMs) exhibit inverse scaling at the subtask level: specific question categories on which larger models perform worse than smaller counterparts within the same model family. We evaluate 19 models from four distinct model families across eight multimodal benchmarks (nine evaluation splits), answering 29,386 questions per model, 558,334 model-question evaluations in total. Using per-question pairwise analysis across all model pairs in each family, we identify 375 subtask-model-pair combinations exhibiting inverse scaling, spanning 4,342 unique queries where a smaller model answers correctly but a larger model fails, and we find that these patterns replicate across independently developed architectures. translated_title: 关于规模的极限：视觉-语言模型中的逆缩放现象
translated_abstract: 缩放定律表明，增加模型规模、训练数据和计算量通常会带来单调递增的性能提升。虽然这在总体层面上往往成立，但我们提出了系统性证据，表明视觉-语言模型在子任务层面表现出“逆缩放”现象：即在同一个模型家族内，较大模型在特定问题类别上的表现反而不如较小的模型。我们评估了来自四个不同模型家族的19个模型，涵盖八个多模态基准（九个评估划分），每个模型回答29,386个问题，总计558,334次模型-问题评估。通过对每个家族内所有模型对进行逐问题的成对分析，我们识别出375个表现出逆缩放现象的子任务-模型对组合，涉及4,342个独特查询——在这些查询中，较小的模型能够正确回答而较大的模型却失败了。此外，我们发现这些模式在独立开发的架构之间也能复现。
tldr: 该论文首次系统性地揭示了视觉-语言模型在子任务层面存在“逆缩放”现象——同一家族中更大的模型在特定问题类别上反而表现更差，并通过大规模评估（19个模型、55万余次评估）识别出375个逆缩放组合，且这些模式在不同独立开发的架构间可复现。
